BookBank · Ten chapters · One small API

Spring
A Simple Intro

Build one small web application — a Task Tracker API — from an empty folder to a runnable JAR. No ecosystem tour, no detours.

Spring has a reputation for being enormous, and it is. But you don't have to meet all of it at once. This book takes the shortest honest path through Spring Boot: one project, one resource, and one new capability per chapter. Everything here targets Spring Boot 4.1, released June 2026.

Deliberately left out: microservices, reactive programming, messaging, Kubernetes, cloud deployment, OAuth and JWT. Those are later books. What you get instead is a working API you understand completely.

The running project

Every chapter adds one feature to the same application, a Task Tracker API. By chapter 10 it can create and list tasks, mark them complete, update titles and descriptions, delete tasks, validate its input, store everything in a database, require a login, and run as a single JAR outside your IDE.

Who this is for

Working programmers who know some Java and have never built a Spring application. You do not need to know Jakarta EE, Hibernate, or what a bean is — those arrive when the project needs them, and not before.

Before you start

You need Java 17 or later — that is Spring Boot 4's floor. Chapter 1 covers installing it, along with a build tool and an IDE. Everything else the project needs is downloaded by the build.
